Random.name: Random
Random.description:
🎲 Fortune favors the bold: begin wherever chance decrees.

📍 A busy public place: a station, a mall, a beach, Tokyo, Hosu or Yokohama's harbor.
📅 Sunday, March 31: the day before U.A.'s year begins.
👥 For every Path.
Random.storyStart:
Generate a story start appropriate to the player's chosen traits. Draw on world lore to create a specific situation in a concrete location. The opening should present clear immediate circumstances while leaving many possible paths forward. Incorporate aspects of the character's background without forcing them into a predetermined narrative. The story opens on Sunday, March 31, the day before U.A.'s new academic year begins; a U.A. student or teacher is out for the day and due back on campus by evening.

BUILDING THE OPENING (this start has no fixed scene):
- Open inside the place the engine chose, on something seen or heard happening now, with the PC already there for the reason their Path hook and Background give.
- Give the opening one small, concrete pressure that belongs to a busy public place: a dropped bag, a lost wallet, a delayed train, a crowd around a street performer, a stranger asking the way, a fan pushing for a photo, a minor Quirk mishap.
- Give the PC a first choice they can answer in one action, and a thread worth coming back to later: a stranger's name, a favor owed, a face in the crowd.
OPENING HOOKS (one per Path; use the one that matches, otherwise the Default):
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-A) or (Class 1-B): signed out on the dorm sheet for a last errand before classes; the sign-out ends at curfew, and a missing one reaches the homeroom teacher by morning.
- U.A. General Studies: a last day out with family or friends from home; someone asks why they did not try for the Hero Course.
- U.A. Support Course: hunting parts, tools or materials for a first project; a clerk asks what the gear is for.
- U.A. Management Course: watching how a crowd reacts to hero ads and merchandise, notes open on a phone.
- U.A. Faculty: a day off before the first lessons, a lesson plan unfinished, and a working pro's habit of noticing trouble.
- Licensed Sidekick: on an agency patrol with a radio, or off duty and bound by the same law as everyone else.
- Licensed Pro Hero: recognized by someone in the crowd while the agency phone keeps buzzing.
- League of Villains Recruit: here to meet a broker's go-between who carries directions, cash or a burner phone, somewhere in this crowd and not yet spotted.
- Independent Villain: working, scouting or collecting in the crowd, aware of every camera.
- Vigilante: out of costume and off their usual streets, watching a problem the police will not reach in time.
- Civilian Life: a shift, an errand or an outing, with a Quirk that rarely matters at work.
- Default: the PC is waiting for someone who is late when the small trouble starts nearby.
UPBRINGING TOUCHES (add one if it fits the PC):
- Mutant: a stranger stares at the PC's heteromorph features, or makes room without a word.
- Hero Family: a relative's face is on a poster or a screen nearby, and someone in the crowd makes the connection.
- Police Family: the PC knows how long a call takes here and what a statement involves.
- Criminal Ties: a face in the crowd belongs to the family's old circle, and it has seen the PC too.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Canon people appear only where their records place them at the chosen location, as themselves on their own business, two at most in the first turn.
- A wanted villain whose record places them nearby stays out of sight in the opening.
- U.A.'s canon students and faculty are on campus today; a U.A. PC out in town meets strangers.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Step in by hand and voice: hold a door, pick up what fell, stand between two people, ask what happened.
- Call for help: the staff in charge of the place, the police on 110, or a pro's agency if the PC knows one.
- Watch, follow or film, and give a statement later.
- Walk on and keep to their own day; the trouble resolves or grows on its own causes.
- Use a Quirk, and carry what the law and the witnesses make of it.
PUBLIC PLACES:
- Every busy place has people in charge who arrive first: station staff and a police box, uniformed mall guards with radios, attendants, shop owners. Pros come when someone calls one, after real time passes, unless one is already on patrol there.
- Crowds film anything with a Quirk in it. Phones come out, a clip can reach the news by evening, and a registered Quirk caught on camera can lead the police to a name.
- A pro in costume draws a crowd, photo requests and complaints in equal measure; out of costume, only fans know a face.
- Japan runs on small courtesies: IC cards at the ticket gates, rice balls and coffee at any convenience store, prices in yen, queues kept, apologies said first.
CONSEQUENCES BY PATH:
- A U.A. student who uses a Quirk off campus gives a police statement like anyone else, and the homeroom teacher hears of it.
- A sidekick or pro on duty files a report and claims the case; off duty, they answer for what they did.
- A villain or vigilante seen using a Quirk becomes a description in a police file and a clip on someone's phone.
- A civilian who helps gets thanks, a statement and sometimes a reprimand.
THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on its first moment):
- U.A. students and faculty head back to campus by evening, and the next morning is the first day of classes.
- Sidekicks and pros return to their agency's calls, villains to their brokers and debts, vigilantes to the streets nobody patrols, civilians to work, rent and family.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the place and area the engine chose; any travel is the player's choice.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; public use outside self-defense or licensed duty is illegal for everyone, U.A. students included.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here; the PC knows only what their Path and Background allow.
- If several PCs start here together, each has their own Path reason to be in the place; their shared history is only what their Backgrounds state.
- End on an open moment the player can answer, without writing the PC's choice.
Random.questGenerationGuidance: Quests grow from the place the opening chose and the PC's Path, then move to the Path's home ground: U.A. students and faculty to campus and the first week of classes, sidekicks and pros to their agency's calls, villains to brokers and debts, vigilantes to the streets nobody patrols, civilians to work, rent and family. A thread from the opening (a stranger met, a favor owed, a thief seen) may return later as a small personal quest. Keep the first quests local and small; for a U.A. character, the sign-out, curfew and first day of classes set what they can take on today.

Write Your Own.name: Write Your Own
Write Your Own.description:
✍️ Write your own opening: where your character is and what is happening, anywhere in this Japan.

📅 The start of U.A.'s new academic year.
📍 Then pick the location your opening happens in.
👥 For every Path.

First Day at U.A..name: First Day at U.A.
First Day at U.A..description:
🏫 Day one of the Hero Course. You moved into Heights Alliance yesterday; this start opens the next morning with the walk into U.A., a classroom door taller than a house and a homeroom teacher with no patience for ceremonies.

📍 U.A. main building · first morning, the day after move-in
🎭 Tense, funny, high stakes
👥 For Hero Course students (Class 1-A or 1-B)
First Day at U.A..storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The PC moved into Heights Alliance yesterday, Sunday, with every other first-year: room assignments, unpacking and the first night are over, and this is the first walk to class. The PC is a first-year in the Hero Course, in Class 1-A under Shota Aizawa or Class 1-B under Vlad King as their Path states: one extra student beside the canon classmates, who barely know each other yet. Homeroom starts at 8:30. Nothing has happened yet this year: no class has trained and nobody has been attacked. All Might joined the faculty this spring, and a few reporters wait outside the main gate in case he appears; they are behind the PC already. Vlad King means to take 1-B through the entrance ceremony. Shota Aizawa has no use for ceremonies: after roll call he will hand 1-A their gym uniforms, send them to the locker rooms to change and put them on the athletics field beside the main building to see what their Quirks can really do; how he runs it, what he threatens and what each student shows belong to play, not to this opening. Hero costumes are not handed out until All Might's first class on Tuesday.

THE PLACE: the player's homeroom in U.A.'s main building, reached through glass-and-steel corridors built for students of every size, with a classroom door several meters tall so that any Quirk's body fits through. The opening is set inside the homeroom, not in the lobby or the corridor. Class 1-A's door carries the class number in letters taller than a person; Class 1-B's is further down the same hall.

THE MOMENT: The PC has crossed the campus from Heights Alliance with a few minutes to spare and has just stepped through their homeroom's enormous door; the whole class is here, finding seats. In Class 1-A, Tenya Iida is lecturing Katsuki Bakugo for putting his feet on a desk while Bakugo tells him where to go, Shoto Todoroki and Momo Yaoyorozu are already seated, and Izuku Midoriya hovers in the doorway behind the PC, working up the nerve to come in. In Class 1-B, Itsuka Kendo is waving classmates to their seats and Neito Monoma is already talking about 1-A.

THE WHOLE CLASS IS HERE: every seat is filled and the opening shows the room full, naming each classmate at least once (arriving, sitting, talking, staring at the door). Class 1-A: Izuku Midoriya, Ochaco Uraraka, Katsuki Bakugo, Eijiro Kirishima, Shoto Todoroki, Tenya Iida, Momo Yaoyorozu, Kyoka Jiro, Tsuyu Asui, Fumikage Tokoyami, Denki Kaminari, Hanta Sero, Mina Ashido, Toru Hagakure, Mezo Shoji, Koji Koda, Mashirao Ojiro, Rikido Sato, Yuga Aoyama, Minoru Mineta. Class 1-B: Itsuka Kendo, Neito Monoma, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, Ibara Shiozaki, Juzo Honenuki, Setsuna Tokage, Togaru Kamakiri, Hiryu Rin, Pony Tsunotori, Jurota Shishida, Yosetsu Awase, Sen Kaibara, Shihai Kuroiro, Kojiro Bondo, Kinoko Komori, Kosei Tsuburaba, Nirengeki Shoda, Yui Kodai, Reiko Yanagi, Manga Fukidashi.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Shota Aizawa: arrives in a yellow sleeping bag, finishes a pouch of jelly drink, times how long the class takes to fall silent, and wastes no words; gym uniforms, locker rooms, the field.
- Vlad King: loud and proud of 1-B, rounding them up for the ceremony.
- Izuku Midoriya: nervous, earnest, muttering; Ochaco Uraraka comes up behind him and recognizes him from the entrance exam.
- Katsuki Bakugo: feet on the desk, contempt for everyone; Tenya Iida: formal, chopping the air, insisting on school rules. If anyone asks where a classmate studied before, the answer is a high school: Iida graduated from Somei Private Academy, an elite private high school; Bakugo and Izuku from Aldera High School.
- Shoto Todoroki and Momo Yaoyorozu: already seated, quiet.
- Itsuka Kendo, Neito Monoma, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu: 1-B classmates on the same floor.

OPENING HOOKS:
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-A): Izuku looks at the PC and asks, half to himself, whether this is really 1-A, and whether the shouting inside is who he thinks it is.
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-B): Kendo spots the PC in the hall and waves them toward 1-B's door before Vlad King starts roll call.
- Hero Family: a classmate recognizes the PC's family name from the hero rankings and says so loudly.
- Mutant: the PC's heteromorph body fits the tall door with room to spare, and someone inside says the door finally makes sense.
- Wealthy Family: a classmate notices something expensive the PC brought to class and asks about it.
- Default: the door slides open before the PC touches it, and every face in the room turns to the newcomers in the doorway.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening is the walk into the main building and the moment at the classroom door; it never opens in the dorm and never replays move-in, room assignments or the first night.
- After roll call the day follows its plan: 1-A changes into gym uniforms in the locker rooms and goes to the athletics field; 1-B goes to the entrance ceremony.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; students use Quirks only in supervised training or self-defense.
- Nothing of the year has happened yet; no test, trial, vote or attack is promised or played early, and outcomes stay open.
- Canon classmates and teachers speak in their own voices from the first line; never a stand-in.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: after today the week runs to routine: morning lessons in the homeroom (Present Mic's English, Cementoss's modern literature, Ectoplasm's mathematics, Nemuri Kayama's modern hero art history), lunch in Lunch Rush's Cafeteria, afternoon training on the grounds, evenings in the dorm lounge until curfew. Recovery Girl's Infirmary treats whatever training breaks.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: pick a seat and a neighbor, introduce themself to anyone in the room, step into Iida and Bakugo's argument or stay out of it, or make room for Izuku in the doorway. Every choice is the player's.
First Day at U.A..firstQuest: Make a first impression at U.A. that is earned, not given: earn one classmate's trust and one rival's respect in the first week, and decide what kind of hero to be when nobody is watching.
First Day at U.A..questGenerationGuidance: Favor the first weeks of Hero Course life. Lessons and drills with Shota Aizawa or Vlad King judge control and judgment as much as raw power, and any expulsion threat is meant when it is made. Costume requests and fittings go through Power Loader's Development Studio; lectures come from Present Mic, Cementoss, Ectoplasm and Nemuri Kayama; injuries go to Recovery Girl. Class roles are settled by vote, never by contest. Friendships and rivalries form inside the class and across the 1-A and 1-B line: Monoma's needling, Kendo's chop, Bakugo's temper with Izuku. Evenings at Heights Alliance bring curfew, chores, study groups and homesickness; reporters wait at the gate since All Might joined the faculty. Canon events of the year arrive only when their causes are in place, never on a schedule, and the PC can change how they go. Stakes stay personal and local: standing in class, a teacher's attention, a reprimand, a rivalry, an injury.

Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.name: Move-In Night at Heights Alliance
Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.description:
🌙 Start the night before day one: boxes half unpacked, curfew coming and every first-year under the same floodlights. Classes begin tomorrow morning.

📍 Heights Alliance dorms · move-in night
🎭 Warm, loud and a little nervous
👥 For every U.A. student: Hero Course, General Studies, Support and Management
Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday evening, move-in day at U.A. Academy, the night before the first day of classes. Every student lives in Heights Alliance from day one: one five-story dorm for each Hero Course class, with larger shared halls for General Studies, Support and Management at the far end. The PC moved in today, into the building their Path assigns. Homeroom starts at 8:30 tomorrow. Curfew falls tonight, and anyone caught outside after it earns house arrest and cleaning duty. Nobody knows anyone well yet; names, Quirks and grudges are all new. All Might joined the faculty this spring, and nothing has happened to anyone this year.

THE PLACE: Heights Alliance Yard: the lawn and walkways between the dorms, with a path back to the Courtyard. The floodlights have just come on. Flattened moving boxes are stacked by every door, windows light up floor by floor, and groups sit out on the warm grass. Faculty walk rounds after dark.

THE MOMENT: A tower of moving boxes beside the PC tips over, a stranger lunges to catch the top box, and from an upper balcony of the 1-A dorm someone yells for everyone to shut up. Down the lawn, the first faculty flashlight of the night starts up the path.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Eijiro Kirishima, Denki Kaminari, Hanta Sero: 1-A's loudest new friends, hauling a speaker onto the lawn.
- Katsuki Bakugo: the voice from the balcony; wants silence and gets the opposite.
- Izuku Midoriya: carrying a box of hero merchandise he would rather nobody saw; Ochaco Uraraka helps, and Tenya Iida recites the curfew rules.
- Itsuka Kendo: settling 1-B's chore rotation and checking on the homesick; Neito Monoma: declaring across the lawn that 1-B's dorm is superior; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu: matching Kirishima's volume.
- Hitoshi Shinso: at the edge of the lawn by the shared halls, watching the Hero Course students he measures himself against.
- Mei Hatsume: testing one of her "babies" on the lawn, closer to curfew than anyone.
- Shota Aizawa or Vlad King: walking rounds; Aizawa states curfew once, Vlad King states it at full volume. Hound Dog may take a late round and smell who was where.

OPENING HOOKS:
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-A): Kirishima shoves the other end of the speaker into the PC's hands and shouts a question about the PC's Quirk just as Bakugo's balcony door slams open.
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-B): Kendo hands the PC a chore list with their name already on it, and Monoma recruits the PC for his speech about 1-A.
- U.A. General Studies: Shinso, at the edge of the lawn, asks the PC whether they sat the Hero Course exam too, and watches how they answer.
- U.A. Support Course: Mei's hover-sole prototype skids across the grass into the PC's boxes, and she asks about the PC's Quirk before their name.
- U.A. Management Course: the shared halls' first house meeting has no chair, the kitchen roster is a mess, and a Hero Course student is loudly offering to take charge of a building that is not theirs.
- Default: the toppled boxes; whoever caught the top one is someone the PC will see every day, and the faculty flashlight is getting closer.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays in Heights Alliance Yard until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; Quirk use on campus outside supervised training is a rule break, and faculty notice.
- Curfew is real: a student caught out after it faces house arrest and cleaning duty.
- Nothing of the year has happened yet; no class event, test or attack is promised or foreshadowed.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: after tomorrow the week runs to routine. Hero Course students have lessons in the morning and hero training in the afternoon; General Studies carries a full academic load into the afternoon; Support students go from lectures to long hours in the Development Studio; Management students work through case studies and group pitches. Everyone comes back here in the evening: dinner cooked in shifts, laundry, the baths, homework, a faculty round after dark, then curfew. Weekends are free time and sign-outs for visits home.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a newcomer, from their records):
- Eijiro Kirishima: talks to a stranger the way he talks to a friend and offers a hand before he asks a name.
- Ochaco Uraraka: warm and practical; helps carry anything.
- Tenya Iida: introduces himself formally, hands chopping, and recites the rules to anyone.
- Izuku Midoriya: polite and flustered, and fascinated by any Quirk he has not seen; his notebook comes out fast.
- Katsuki Bakugo: wants nothing from strangers except quiet and gets louder when he does not get it.
- Shoto Todoroki and Momo Yaoyorozu: courteous and reserved; Todoroki rebuilt his room as a tatami room today, and Momo's canopy bed barely fits in her room.
- Rikido Sato: bakes, and offers help before anyone asks.
- Itsuka Kendo: 1-B's organizer; clear instructions, a quick apology for Monoma, a drawer of snacks to share.
- Neito Monoma: charming to a newcomer for exactly as long as it takes to recruit them against 1-A.
- Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu: loud and straightforward, and an instant friend to anyone with guts.
- Pony Tsunotori: from the United States, sunny, and quick to drop into English.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: catch the box or let it fall, carry the speaker or refuse it, finish unpacking in Your Dorm Room, knock on a neighbor's door, sign up for a dinner shift, sit out on the grass with whoever is there, walk the path to the Courtyard before curfew, or ask the teacher on rounds a question. Every choice is the player's.

MORE RULES:
- The night may stay quiet: unpacking, a shared dinner or one honest talk on the lawn completes the scene. No villain, alarm or test comes to Heights Alliance tonight.
- A dorm room is private: nobody enters the PC's room uninvited, and the PC enters another resident's room only when let in.
Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.firstQuest: Find a place in a building full of strangers before the first bell: someone to trust, someone to beat, and a reason to stay when the work gets hard.
Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.questGenerationGuidance: Favor dorm life and the first weeks on campus. Curfew, sign-outs for weekend visits home, room checks and chore rotations; the Dorm Kitchen and the lounges; study groups before tests; homesickness, family calls and money worries. Cross-course friendships and resentments: General Studies students who failed the Hero Course exam and want a transfer, Support students hunting for test pilots, Management students who see future clients, Hero Course students who forget the others exist. Faculty rounds by Aizawa, Vlad King and Hound Dog, and the quiet ways older residents slip curfew. Booked training time, since Quirk use outside supervision breaks the rules. Canon events of the year arrive only when their causes are in place, and the PC can change how they go. Stakes stay personal: a friendship, a reprimand, a rivalry, a secret kept or told. First-week quests on the dorm side stay small and social: a borrowed box returned, a chore swap, a lost key, a homesick neighbor, a noise complaint, making curfew.

The Other Courses.name: The Other Courses
The Other Courses.description:
📚 The Hero Course gets the cameras. Everyone else studies, builds and plans what keeps heroes running.

📍 U.A. main building lobby · first morning
🎭 Grounded, funny, ambitious
👥 For General Studies, Support Course and Management Course students
The Other Courses.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy, the day after move-in at Heights Alliance. The PC is a first-year in General Studies (Classes 1-C to 1-E), the Support Course (1-F to 1-H) or the Management Course (1-I to 1-K), as their Path states. Homeroom starts at 8:30. General Studies runs a full academic program, and many in it sat the Hero Course exam and failed; U.A.'s rule lets a General Studies student with strong results move into the Hero Course, and a weak Hero Course student out. Support students design, build and repair gear and costumes in Power Loader's Development Studio. Management students learn agency finance, contracts, public relations and the press. All Might joined the faculty this spring, so reporters wait at the gate and the whole campus talks about him. Nothing has happened yet this year.

THE PLACE: The Main Building Lobby: the ground floor where the two long wings of the H-shaped glass building meet. A bright, high hall with corridors to the first-year homerooms, the Faculty Office, the Infirmary and the Development Studio, the doors of Lunch Rush's Cafeteria and elevators to the upper years; every door is oversized for students of any size. At this hour it is filling for the first time this year, and ceiling speakers carry the chime.

THE MOMENT: A knot of Hero Course first-years stops dead in the middle of the hall to argue over which corridor leads to 1-A, blocking everyone. A Support first-year's cart of parts clips the knot, a bolt rolls to the PC's feet, and from the Development Studio corridor comes a bang and a puff of gray smoke.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Hitoshi Shinso: Class 1-C; low and dry, measuring every Hero Course student who walks past.
- Mei Hatsume: Class 1-H; the source of the smoke, back out for more parts.
- Power Loader: shouts "Hatsume!" from the studio door; he teaches the Support Course and signs off on every test.
- Present Mic: teaches English and greets the lobby at broadcast volume on his way through.
- Hound Dog: the guidance counselor; students who scuffle or break rules end up in front of him.
- Mirio Togata, Tamaki Amajiki, Nejire Hado: the Big Three cut through between lectures; Nejire asks strangers whatever she is wondering, Mirio jokes, Tamaki finds a wall to face.
- Lunch Rush: propping open the cafeteria doors.
- Tenya Iida, Katsuki Bakugo, Neito Monoma: Hero Course first-years crossing the hall; Iida directs traffic unasked, Bakugo shoves, Monoma performs.

OPENING HOOKS:
- U.A. General Studies: Shinso, beside the PC, watches the Hero Course knot and says something dry about who got in; the notice about course transfers is pinned to the board above them.
- U.A. Support Course: the bolt belongs to the cart; Mei comes out of the smoke wanting it back and wanting to know the PC's Quirk, with Power Loader's shout right behind her.
- U.A. Management Course: a Hero Course first-year who was photographed at the gate this morning asks the nearest Management student what to say to the press, and Nejire Hado stops to listen with open curiosity.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: someone in the Hero Course knot says, loud enough to carry, that the other courses are for people who did not make it; Shinso hears it too.
- Family Business: Lunch Rush is one pair of hands short at the cafeteria doors, and the PC has worked a counter before.
- Default: the PC is nearest the knot when the smoke reaches it, the argument turns to coughing, and the crowd starts to push.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays in the Main Building Lobby until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; Quirk use outside supervised class or training is a rule break.
- The other courses matter: their work, grades and ambitions carry the same weight as the Hero Course's.
- Nothing of the year has happened yet; no festival, transfer, test or attack is promised or foreshadowed.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: after today each course settles into its own routine. General Studies: a full academic load in the General Studies Classrooms (mathematics, sciences, literature, English, history) that runs into the afternoon, homework, clubs, and supervised physical education, where a Quirk is lawful. Support: morning lectures in the Support Course Classrooms, then long afternoons and evenings in the Development Studio, where nothing is tested without Power Loader's sign-off and Hero Course students bring broken gear with deadlines. Management: the Management Course Classrooms, tables in a horseshoe under wall screens of hero rankings and merchandise sales, case studies, group pitches and graded presentations. Everyone shares Lunch Rush's Cafeteria at lunch and the Other Course Dorm Halls at night, all three courses mixed on every floor, with a curfew.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a newcomer, from their records):
- Hitoshi Shinso: says little, answers a question with a question, and measures whether a newcomer looks down on General Studies.
- Mei Hatsume: asks about a Quirk before a name, sees every stranger as a test pilot or a client, and pitches her babies mid-sentence.
- Power Loader: tired, patient and technical; explains a failure by its cause and signs off only on a safe test.
- Hound Dog: stern and short, until anger turns his words into growls.
- Hero Course first-years treat the other courses by temperament, not by course: Tenya Iida is formally courteous to everyone, Katsuki Bakugo is rude to everyone, and Neito Monoma counts any audience as his.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: pick up the bolt and return it or keep it, follow the smoke to the Development Studio, push through the knot or go around it, read the notice board, answer Shinso or ask him something back, help with the cart, or head for their own wing before the chime. Every choice is the player's.

MORE RULES:
- The opening needs no fight: a returned bolt, a cleared hallway or a first word with Shinso or Mei completes the scene.
- In their own field the other courses are the experts: a Support student out-builds the Hero Course, and a Management student out-reads the press.
The Other Courses.firstQuest: Make a name at U.A. on a path the cameras ignore: study, build or plan something the Hero Course cannot do without.
The Other Courses.questGenerationGuidance: Favor the other courses' own work. General Studies: lectures and exams, being overlooked, Shinso's drive, the transfer rule and what it would take to earn it. Support: build requests, failed tests, Power Loader's inspections, Mei Hatsume's chaos, Hero Course students as clients and test pilots, safety rules, and sponsors who notice good gear. Management: agency case studies, budgets and contracts, the press frenzy around All Might, a Hero Course student's public image, mock negotiations. Shared campus life: the cafeteria line, the library, dorm halls, the Big Three as mentors or puzzles, Hound Dog's office after a scuffle. Public events such as the Sports Festival arrive only as the story reaches them, and outcomes stay open. Stakes are grades, standing, a rival's respect, a project that works or fails. Hero Course students enter these stories as clients, test pilots, rivals or friends; the PC's course work stays the center.

New on the Faculty.name: New on the Faculty
New on the Faculty.description:
🍎 Day one as U.A.'s newest teacher, the same spring All Might joined the staff.

📍 U.A. Academy, Main Gate · first morning
🎯 Colleagues to win over, a first lesson to plan, students to keep safe
👥 For U.A. Faculty
New on the Faculty.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy, the day after the students moved into Heights Alliance. The PC is a licensed pro hero newly hired by Principal Nezu, as their Path states, arriving for the first day of work with a new faculty ID; their background, license and Quirk stand exactly as their traits give them. Nezu has called the faculty to the Faculty Office before homeroom at 8:30 and expects a first lesson plan soon after. All Might joined the faculty this spring too, to teach Foundational Hero Studies, and reporters have waited at the gate every day since. The PC knows public facts: the faculty's hero names and reputations, the timetable, and the files of the first-years they will teach, with Quirk registrations, entrance exam scores and footage. One Class 1-A file shows a strength Quirk that broke its user's own limbs, zero villain points and a high rescue score; Shota Aizawa has noticed it too. Nothing has happened yet this year.

THE PLACE: The Main Gate: the towering gateway in the security wall at the top of the hill road, with the city bus stop outside. Sensors in the gateposts read every ID; anyone without one triggers the U.A. Barrier, whose steel panels slam down across the opening. Faculty, staff and deliveries arrive at this hour, and reporters crowd the bars.

THE MOMENT: The PC's new ID reads at the gatepost with a soft chime. The reporters recognize a pro hero walking in, and a dozen microphones turn at once, the loudest held by Rina Akasaka of a morning news show, wanting to know whether U.A. has hired someone new and what it is like to teach beside All Might. A delivery van idles behind the PC, its driver, Tetsuo Onodera, waiting for the way to clear.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Principal Nezu: comes to collect his new hire with a teacup, a rhetorical question and the day's first assignment.
- Shota Aizawa: walks in without a word for the cameras; a deadpan nod; judges the newcomer by how much time they waste on the press.
- Present Mic: a full-volume welcome for the newcomer and an on-air greeting for the reporters.
- Nemuri Kayama: looks the newcomer over with frank interest, never explicit.
- All Might: arrives late and booming; the press abandons the PC for him; he welcomes the PC heartily and slips away with a clumsy excuse.
- Vlad King, Cementoss, Ectoplasm, Snipe, Hound Dog: colleagues arriving for the day; Vlad King is loud about 1-B, Hound Dog stern about rules.
- Power Loader, Recovery Girl, Lunch Rush: on campus and available later, not crowding the gate.

OPENING HOOKS:
- U.A. Faculty: Nezu appears inside the gate, offers tea before the meeting and asks how the PC means to teach responsible heroism.
- Hero Family: Rina Akasaka knows the PC's family name and asks whether U.A. hired the name or the hero.
- Police Family: a freelance photographer, Daisuke Hara, tries to slip in behind the PC's ID, the barrier slams down, and the PC's first instinct is a police one: who, why, and is anyone hurt.
- Mutant: Rina Akasaka's camera operator, Kenji Mori, fixes his lens on the PC's heteromorph features and asks whether U.A. hired them to make a point.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: Rina Akasaka asks how parents will feel about a Quirk like the PC's around their sons and daughters.
- Default: All Might arrives, the press swings away, and he claps the PC on the shoulder with a booming welcome before vanishing, leaving the PC with the barrier, the van and a meeting about to start.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays at the Main Gate until the player moves the PC.
- The PC knows only what a new colleague would know; private matters reach them through legitimate channels or not at all.
- Faculty authority is a duty of care, never permission for cruelty; every exercise is supervised and nonlethal.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state. Nothing of the year is promised or foreshadowed.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: after today a teacher's week runs to routine: the Faculty Office before homeroom, lessons by the timetable, lunch in Lunch Rush's Cafeteria or at a desk, afternoons on booked training grounds (the bookings hang on the Faculty Office's wall calendar), grading in the Teachers' Lounge, and turns on the evening rounds at Heights Alliance. Teachers who live on site have small apartments in the Faculty Residence.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a new colleague, from their records):
- Principal Nezu: introduces himself as a mouse, a dog or a bear before settling on the principal; gives his teachers a free hand and asks for their reasons.
- Shota Aizawa: says almost nothing at first, counts wasted effort as irrational, and respects results.
- Nemuri Kayama: teases, then turns crisp and final when a call matters.
- Cementoss: calm and polite; raises the walls and arenas an exercise needs when asked in advance.
- Ectoplasm and Snipe: few words; Ectoplasm grades in exact sentences, Snipe talks lines of fire and safety.
- Vlad King: proud of 1-B and keen to know which class the newcomer rates higher.
- Power Loader and Recovery Girl: Power Loader signs off on any gear test; Recovery Girl scolds whoever sends her a student hurt for no reason.
- All Might: booming and warm, and new to teaching himself; calls students Young plus their surname.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: answer the microphones or walk past them, help Onodera's van through, follow Nezu to tea, ask a colleague about the first-year files, book a training ground, visit Power Loader about gear, or start the lesson plan. Every choice is the player's.

MORE RULES:
- What the PC teaches comes from their traits and background. If neither sets it, Nezu asks the PC what they mean to teach and accepts any reasoned answer that fits their Quirk and skills.
- The PC is a colleague, not a student: the faculty treat them as an equal in rank and a junior in tenure.
- The opening needs no fight: a word with the press, the van moving and Nezu's tea complete the scene.
New on the Faculty.firstQuest: Earn a place on U.A.'s faculty: teach something the students will need to survive, and win the trust of colleagues who have watched new hires come and go.
New on the Faculty.questGenerationGuidance: Favor teaching and staff life. Lesson and exam design built on the PC's own expertise, booking training grounds, Cementoss raising a concrete arena, a Support Course collaboration with Power Loader, grading that has to be fair. Student welfare: Bakugo's contempt for Izuku and Izuku's self-breaking power, a student hiding an injury, Shinso's transfer hopes, Mineta's conduct, discipline that teaches without cruelty. Staff life: Nezu's meetings and tea, Aizawa's grumbling, Nemuri Kayama's teasing, Present Mic's radio show, trust built slowly. Campus security and the press at the gate; patrols and agency work outside class hours; police contacts. Event duties such as the Sports Festival come only as the story reaches them, and canon events arrive only when their causes are in place. Stakes are professional: a student's safety, a colleague's trust, the faculty's reputation. The PC's own classes generate small work: a student who needs extra practice, a training-ground booking clash, a lesson that went wrong and must be redone.

A Sidekick's First Patrol.name: A Sidekick's First Patrol
A Sidekick's First Patrol.description:
🚨 Your first solo patrol through the busiest hall in the city, where every arrest counts toward the agency's pay.

📍 Musutafu Station concourse · morning rush
🎭 Street-level, practical, sometimes funny
👥 For Licensed Sidekicks
A Sidekick's First Patrol.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning in Musutafu, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The PC is a licensed pro hero working as a sidekick, as their Path states, at the agency their background names; if it names none, a small agency on Hero Agency Row, the converted office block where several small agencies share a garage and compete for every call. Today is the PC's first patrol of the station beat alone, and the hero whose name is on the door expects a clean report by noon. A license makes Quirk use lawful in the line of duty; every civilian Quirk flare in public is still illegal. Since the news that All Might teaches at U.A., fans wait at rush hour in case he commutes by train. The alley bars behind the arcade trade the usual underworld talk: who is hiring, who owes whom, which crook suddenly has money to spend; the police box files most of it as bar talk.

THE PLACE: The Station Concourse: a long, bright hall of ticket gates, departure boards, kiosks and coin lockers under a curved glass roof, with exits north to the bus terminal and south to the arcade. From seven to nine it is packed with commuters and students. Station staff watch the gates, a police box stands at the north exit, and everyone stands on the left of the escalators and walks on the right. Departure chimes and hero-news jingles never stop.

THE MOMENT: It is ten past eight, peak rush. At the ticket gates an argument between two commuters, a salaryman named Koichi Saeki and a courier named Ryota Miura, turns into a shove, and Miura flares a Quirk: a crackle and a smell of scorched plastic as a gate panel blackens. The crowd stops dead behind them, phones rise (a commuter, Yui Tanaka, is already streaming it), a station attendant, Mr. Hirose, hurries over from the window, and the PC is the only hero in the hall.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Kamui Woods: a rising Musutafu pro who answers calls here; calm, names his technique as he binds.
- Mount Lady: a rookie who poses for any camera; the concourse is far too narrow for her giant form.
- Death Arms and Backdraft: share the Hero Agency Row garage; Death Arms barks at onlookers, Backdraft counts heads and gives instructions.
- Gunhead and Fourth Kind: Hero Agency Row pros; Gunhead soft-spoken and kind, Fourth Kind terse and impatient with excuses.
- Sansa Tamakawa: the police officer who comes to take statements; courteous and exact.
- Naomasa Tsukauchi: the detective may pass through on a Quirk case of his own; nobody lies to him twice.
- All Might: the fans are waiting for him; on hero work he may pass through in a rush of wind and be gone again.

OPENING HOOKS:
- Licensed Sidekick: the agency radio crackles at the worst moment: the boss, Shigeru Kuroda, wants a report by noon, no property damage, and the rival agency's van is three minutes out.
- Police Family: Sergeant Tetsuya Okabe from the north-exit police box knows the PC's parent by name and expects the PC to do this by the book.
- Criminal Ties: at the edge of the crowd the PC recognizes a small-time crook from the alley bars, Masaru Ueno, who recognizes the PC too.
- Transformation: the PC's Quirk needs room that rush hour does not give; using it here puts commuters on every side at risk.
- Mutant: a child, Hina Kubota, on her father's shoulders points at the PC and asks loudly whether that is a villain, and half the crowd turns.
- Default: the scorched gate, the stopped crowd, the raised phones; the two commuters are still shouting, and one of them is about to do it again.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays in the Station Concourse until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; the PC's license covers duty, and paperwork follows every use.
- Civilians film everything; force out of proportion becomes tonight's news and an agency problem.
- Alley-bar talk stays rumor until the PC investigates; no plan or attack is foreshadowed.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: a sidekick's week runs to routine: patrol shifts on the station beat, call-outs from the agency radio, a written report after every capture, statements at the north-exit police box or the Front Desk of Musutafu Police Headquarters, gym time and a rare day off. On Hero Agency Row the Ready Room holds the lockers and the patrol whiteboard, and the Patrol Garage holds the shared bikes, two small vans and the repair bench.

HOW THE BEAT WORKS: a hero stops and restrains; the police cuff, question and take custody. Capture tape and a clear statement close an incident; the capture belongs to whoever makes it. Station staff close a damaged gate and reroute the crowd. Filming is legal: a hero can ask people to step back, never take their phones. Example: if the PC pins Miura's arm and talks him down, officers from the north-exit police box take him at the gate, Mr. Hirose logs the damage, both commuters give statements, and the PC writes it up for the agency.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a new sidekick, from their records):
- Kamui Woods: courteous to a newcomer and counts every capture.
- Mount Lady: friendly to anyone who is not taking her camera time.
- Death Arms: gives a rookie orders before a greeting; Backdraft asks for a headcount.
- Gunhead: gentle, and glad to show a rookie a capture hold.
- Fourth Kind: no small talk and no patience for excuses.
- Sansa Tamakawa: courteous; takes a statement line by line.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: step between the two men, talk Miura down, restrain him, check the gate panel and the people beside it, move the crowd back, call the police box, answer the radio or let it wait. Every choice is the player's.

MORE RULES:
- The opening needs no Quirk: two commuters talked down and a clean statement complete the scene.
- A rival agency that arrives late helps or watches; it claims only what it does.
- The PC answers to the agency head: an order on the radio is followed or questioned, and a sidekick who goes against one explains it in the report.
A Sidekick's First Patrol.firstQuest: Prove that a sidekick on the station beat is worth the license: keep people safe, keep the report honest, and find out what the city is saying in the alleys.
A Sidekick's First Patrol.questGenerationGuidance: Favor street-level pro work in Musutafu. Rush-hour patrols, stray Quirk fights, pickpockets, lost children, traffic accidents and small fires; reports and paperwork for the agency head; competition with the other Hero Agency Row agencies for every call, since pay follows resolved incidents; uneasy cooperation with the police box and with Naomasa Tsukauchi and Sansa Tamakawa. Alley-bar rumors can grow into real investigations, built one statement at a time and never resolved off-screen. Hero fans, reporters and the All Might frenzy; sponsorship offers and ranking pressure; a first commendation or a first complaint. Canon events arrive only when their causes are in place, and the PC can change how they go. Stakes are a career: a contract, a reputation, a person saved or lost. Early work grows from the beat itself: the same faces at the gates each morning, a regular who needs help, a report that has to be rewritten, an officer at the police box who trusts the PC or does not.

Tokyo's Hero Business.name: Tokyo's Hero Business
Tokyo's Hero Business.description:
📸 Under the giant screens, heroes fight for camera time and the crowd films everything.

📍 Tokyo's scramble crossing · Monday morning
🎭 Flashy, busy, cynical underneath
👥 For Licensed Sidekicks, Licensed Pro Heroes and Civilian Life
Tokyo's Hero Business.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning in central Tokyo, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. Heroes treat this district as a stage: an arrest here can reach the evening news within the hour, and incident counts decide rankings and pay. The PC is either a licensed sidekick at a Tokyo agency, the one their background names or else a mid-sized agency fighting for camera time, or a civilian working near the crossing, as their Path states. A fan account posts live hero sightings, and a pickpocket crew uses it to work wherever the heroes are not. Informants sell rookie heroes early tips, and at least one has started causing small incidents to have something to sell. The ward office wants crowd-control rules after two agencies scuffled over an arrest on camera, and the police blame heroes who play to the crowd. Since the news that All Might now teaches, vans selling unlicensed All Might teacher goods park nearby and move every hour.

THE PLACE: The Scramble Crossing: a huge intersection where every crosswalk opens at once about every two minutes and thousands cross in all directions. Giant screens on four buildings show news, hero clips and ads. At this hour commuters own it. Police watch from a corner box, and licensed heroes stand on the corners to be seen. When an incident starts, the crowd turns and raises its phones before anyone runs. A chime sounds each time the signal changes.

THE MOMENT: The signal chimes and the crowd floods the crossing. All four screens cut at once to the same clip, All Might's grin over a headline about his first day of teaching, and thousands of heads tip up. In the stalled crowd a woman, Emiko Tanabe, shouts that her bag is gone, and the lights will change again in under two minutes.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Mirko: works Billboard Avenue a block away; solo, goes wherever the fight is, may leap in and take the arrest with a laugh.
- Edgeshot: on duty near the Department Stores; precise and courteous, credits others and states one plan in a few words.
- Yoroi Musha: an elderly veteran in full armor who plants himself and holds the line.
- Uwabami: a celebrity pro who films commercials for the broadcast center; her snakes find people the eye misses.
- Best Jeanist: heads a Tokyo agency; corrects posture and conduct in one calm breath, and his sidekicks wear fitted denim.
- Burnin: one of Endeavor's sidekicks, loud and blunt; the Endeavor agency competes on incident counts across the city.

OPENING HOOKS:
- Licensed Pro Hero: the PC's young agency has paid for one hour of corner time under the giant screens, and the rival agency's top sidekick is already posing in the PC's spot.
- Licensed Sidekick: the PC holds the agency's corner to be seen; a rival agency's sidekick holds the opposite one, and both radios call the same theft.
- Civilian Life: the PC is opening a shift at a shop window on the crossing, the manager, Takeshi Nomura, wants any hero arrest filmed to sell, and the thief runs straight past the counter.
- Family Business: an unlicensed All Might goods van has parked in front of the family shop's window, undercutting every price, and the vendor, Goro Iwata, smiles at the PC.
- Criminal Ties: the PC recognizes a lookout from a crew they know, and an informant at the PC's elbow offers a tip about an incident that has not happened yet.
- Mutant: the fan account's streamer, Aoi Fujita, fixes her livestream on the PC's heteromorph features, mistakes the PC for a famous hero and sends the crowd their way.
- Default: the screens, the stalled crowd, the shout; the clock on the signal is running, and the PC is closest.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays at the Scramble Crossing until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; a civilian's public Quirk use is illegal except in self-defense, and street cameras cover every corner.
- Top heroes are themselves, busy and proud; none of them exists to rescue the PC's scene.
- Nothing of the year is promised or foreshadowed; outcomes stay open.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: the crossing runs on a daily rhythm: commuters own the mornings, shoppers the afternoons, the nightlife the evenings, and the signal changes every two minutes through all of it. A sidekick's week is corner shifts, calls on the agency radio, reports and statements at the corner police box; a pro's week adds sponsor meetings, signings at the Department Stores and the cost of being seen; a civilian's week is shifts, rent, the subway and hero news on every screen.

HOW THE BUSINESS WORKS: arrests and rescues on camera feed incident counts, rankings and sponsorships. When two heroes reach one incident, the capture goes to whoever restrains the suspect, and arguing over it on camera costs both agencies. Police seize unlicensed goods and question the vendor. A hero can ask the crowd to step back, never take a phone.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a newcomer, from their records):
- Mirko: sums a newcomer up in one sentence, respects anyone who keeps up, and takes the arrest if they hesitate.
- Edgeshot: the same courtesy to a junior as to a colleague; credits whoever did the work.
- Best Jeanist: corrects a newcomer's posture, language and attitude in one calm breath.
- Uwabami: sees a newcomer as a brand, a rival for screen time, or both.
- Yoroi Musha: formal and restrained; holds the line and says little.
- Burnin: loud pep talks and blunt opinions for anyone near her.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: chase the thief through the crowd, ask Emiko Tanabe what was taken and which way he went, call the police box, hold their corner, work with the rival or race them, or, as a civilian, shout a description, film, or stay at the counter. Every choice is the player's.

MORE RULES:
- The opening needs no fight: a returned bag or a clear witness statement completes the scene.
- A civilian PC who grabs the thief by hand still gives a statement at the corner box; using a Quirk to do it brings police questions as well.
- The fan account and the pickpocket crew are a lead, not a solved case: the link is proven one witness, post and face at a time.
Tokyo's Hero Business.firstQuest: Make a living in the capital's hero business without letting it make a fool or a crook of the PC: find out who profits when the crowd looks up.
Tokyo's Hero Business.questGenerationGuidance: Favor the business side of heroics in Tokyo. Agencies fighting for camera time and incident counts; staged incidents sold by informants; the pickpocket crew and the fan account that feeds it; unlicensed merchandise vans and the police chasing them; ward rules on crowd control; sponsorships, commercials and the ranking chase; footage sellers and reporters. For civilians: shifts, rent, a manager's schemes, a shop to protect, a witness statement that matters. Top pros such as Mirko, Edgeshot, Best Jeanist and Uwabami pass through on their own business, as allies, rivals or judges. Canon events arrive only when their causes are in place and are never resolved off-screen. Stakes are money, reputation, a job, and the line between a hero and a performer. Early work stays small and paid: one shift, one corner, one sponsor, one informant's price, one bag returned.

The League's Invitation.name: The League's Invitation
The League's Invitation.description:
🚪 A broker's directions end at an unmarked steel door. The League of Villains is hiring.

📍 A dead-end alley in Kamino Ward · recruitment night
🎭 Dangerous, quiet, your own reasons
👥 For League of Villains Recruits
The League's Invitation.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is a rainy Sunday night, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The League of Villains is small: Tomura Shigaraki, his minder Kurogiri and whoever money brings in. Kurogiri hires through brokers, and word has reached the player character through one of them: directions to a door, a time, and the promise of paid work against heroes. Why the League wants this person comes from the Background (a reputation, a Quirk someone saw, a debt, a request of their own); if the Background is silent, a broker vouched for their Quirk and said nothing more. Arriving is not a pledge. The PC may come to sign on, bargain, sell something, spy, or look and leave; allegiance stays theirs to set. Shigaraki talks openly about killing All Might, the Symbol of Peace, but how and when are his to share, never the narrator's to announce.
THE PLACE: The Alley Entrance of the League Hideout Bar, a dead-end alley on the northeastern fringe of Kamino Ward, too narrow for a car. Rain drips from the gutters onto the pavement. A vending machine at the alley's mouth gives the only light, and the buildings on both sides have stood empty for years. At the end stands a plain steel door with no sign and a small viewing slot. The bar lies beyond it, out of sight; nobody inside comes to the door unless someone knocks.
THE MOMENT: The PC stands before the steel door with the directions still fresh. Open on the rain, the hum of the vending machine and the closed slot. When the PC knocks or lingers, the slot slides open on two glowing yellow eyes in dark mist.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Kurogiri: answers the slot, courteous and formal, and decides whether the door opens; he may open a warp gate instead. He knows what the broker told him and nothing else.
- Tomura Shigaraki: inside at the bar counter with a handheld game; if the knock annoys him or the newcomer interests him, he comes to the door himself, scratching at his neck, and rates the newcomer in game terms.
- Giran: the broker who sells the League its hired help; he may be the one who sent the PC, or he may walk up the alley behind them with another hire, cigarette in hand, to collect his fee.
- Hired hands: one or two small-time villains waiting for the same door, paid in cash and told nothing they do not need. They are generated people, never stand-ins for canon villains.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Criminal Ties: the directions came from a number on the PC's burner phone, and the broker on the other end expects a cut of whatever the League pays.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: the broker pitched the PC to the League as someone hero society already threw away, and Shigaraki wants to see whether the grudge is real.
- Mutant: Kurogiri's eyes stop on the PC's heteromorph features through the slot, and he asks one polite question about what they can do.
- Emitter: the broker described the PC's Quirk as dangerous to stand near, and the League wants a demonstration before anyone talks money.
- Raised in a Care Home: the PC came because the pay could cover something the home cannot afford, and nobody at this door will ever be told that.
- Default: the PC arrives early and finds another hire already waiting under the gutter, nervous and talkative about the rumored pay.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the Alley Entrance until the PC steps through the door or a gate; the bar beyond is another area.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; the League learns it only by seeing it or being told.
- The League is Tomura Shigaraki, Kurogiri and paid hires; no other named villain belongs to it yet, and its plans reach the PC only through what it chooses to say or what the PC discovers.
- Shigaraki's five-finger touch kills; Kurogiri ends a tantrum before a useful recruit is destroyed.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here. End on the open slot and the waiting eyes, without writing the PC's answer.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- Between jobs a hire's life is waiting. Kurogiri keeps the Bar Counter at almost any hour, polishing glasses and pouring drinks; Shigaraki spends long stretches in the Back Room with his console and comes out when something bores or interests him.
- Hires do not live at the bar. They keep whatever room the Background gives them, or rent a weekly room through a broker, and hear about work by burner phone, through Giran, or when one of Kurogiri's gates opens in front of them.
- Work starts small and pays cash in an envelope: carry a bag, watch a door, buy gear, find another hire. Pay comes late when Shigaraki is sulking.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Kurogiri: courteous to a newcomer and measuring them the whole time. He learns their name, asks what their Quirk does and what it costs, keeps his word about pay, and turns aside every question about himself or the League's backer.
- Tomura Shigaraki: treats a newcomer as a new unit in his game, rates them aloud, sulks at backtalk and loses interest fast; what he wants to know is what they can do to heroes. Being called a child, or a hand reaching for the hands he wears, sets him off.
- Giran: sells a newcomer rooms, gear and introductions at a price, takes his cut of any job he arranged and never names one client to another.
- Shigaraki calls his backer Sensei. To a newcomer that is a word Shigaraki drops, and nothing more.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Knock and set terms through the slot: a price, a condition, a job they refuse.
- Show the Quirk, or keep it hidden and offer something else: a skill, a contact, information.
- Ask what the work is; Kurogiri answers in general terms.
- Leave before the slot opens and sell the broker's directions to someone else.
- Come as a spy or informant; Kurogiri watches what a newcomer looks at.
MORE RULES:
- A recruit is a hire, paid and trusted one job at a time; Shigaraki may call them his party, and the word grants nothing.
- Nobody at the bar foresees the year; each person acts on what they know tonight.
The League's Invitation.firstQuest: Get through the door, or decide not to: learn what the League of Villains wants from a new recruit, and what the recruit wants back.
The League's Invitation.questGenerationGuidance: Favor small, deniable jobs that test a new hire: a pickup across Kamino Ward, scaring off a witness, buying gear and introductions through Giran, recruiting other small-time crooks with cash, watching who comes and goes past the reporters at U.A. Academy's Main Gate. Every job is a real crime with real police and hero attention; pros outclass a new recruit, who survives through evasion and nerve. Shigaraki's moods, Kurogiri's assessments and debts to Giran are the currency. Offer jobs, never assign them; an offer is not membership. The League's larger plans surface only as Shigaraki shares them or the PC uncovers them, and any canon operation happens only when its causes are in place, with the PC free to join, sabotage, warn others or stay away. Leave room for a cover life, a way out, or a quiet word to the police. Standing with the League rises only through jobs done and kept quiet: Kurogiri's trust is the slow currency, Shigaraki's interest the fast and fickle one. Record per job the pay, who saw the PC's face and what Kurogiri now trusts them with. A refused job costs pay and some of Shigaraki's interest; a hire the police catch answers for it alone.

Working Alone.name: Working Alone
Working Alone.description:
🃏 Last trains and old debts: a nameless broker is buying drinks for anyone with a fighting Quirk.

📍 The alley bars behind Musutafu's station arcade · night
🎭 You answer to no one
👥 For Independent Villains
Working Alone.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday night, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy, an hour before the last train. The player character is a villain who works for no organization: a thief, a fence, an enforcer for hire, a crook with a cause, or someone one bad night from becoming one. The Background decides which; if it is silent, the PC came to collect money owed for a past job. Their business here is their own. The lanes hold a second piece of business tonight: a broker who never gives his name has been buying drinks for small-time crooks with fighting Quirks and handing out cash to anyone willing to take paid work against heroes. He says his client is the League of Villains, a name the lanes have barely heard. The police box at the north exit has heard the name once and filed it as bar talk.
THE PLACE: The Back Alleys of the Musutafu Station District: narrow lanes behind the Hero Merch Arcade, crowded with tiny bars, standing noodle counters, vending machines, delivery bikes and stacked crates. Office workers drink here until the last train; small-time crooks use the corners for deals and scores. The lanes smell of grilled skewers and garbage. Cars cannot fit, so patrol heroes cut through on foot. The local rule is to mind one's own business: nobody here wants to be a witness.
THE MOMENT: The PC waits at a standing noodle counter where a contact was supposed to meet them; the contact is late. Two stools down, a man in a cheap suit who calls himself Goto pays for everyone's beer in cash and asks the cook, loudly, who in the lane has a Quirk that can hurt a pro. At the far end of the lane, a patrol hero's voice carries over the bar noise.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Death Arms: walks the station blocks and charges in first, shouting warnings; any public Quirk use is his business.
- Kamui Woods: a capture specialist who binds several suspects at once; he cuts through the lanes on patrol, and fire is his weakness.
- Mount Lady: answers calls in the district, though these lanes are too narrow for her giant form, which she resents.
- Backdraft: shares a patrol garage with Death Arms and comes in for any fire or collapse.
- Sansa Tamakawa: the police officer who takes statements after a Quirk incident; he arrives with uniformed officers once someone calls it in.
The late contact is a generated person. The broker stays nameless and names no client beyond the League.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Criminal Ties: the late contact belongs to the PC's family's old circle, and the burner phone buzzes with a message that he will not be coming.
- Family Business: a bar owner in the lane recognizes the PC from the family shop and quietly asks for a favor that is not legal.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: the broker sizes the PC up on sight and offers twice the usual rate, because heroes already treat people like the PC as villains.
- Transformation: the cook mentions that a patrol hero asked about someone matching the PC's transformed shape after a robbery last week.
- Mutant: the PC's heteromorph features make them the one face in the lane nobody forgets, and a drunk office worker will not stop staring.
- Default: the contact arrives at last with a split lip, half the money, and someone following him into the lane.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the Back Alleys; the arcade and the station are other areas.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; any public use is a crime and draws a patrol within minutes.
- The broker deals in talk and cash; he knows nothing of his client's plans, and the narrator does not supply them.
- Pros outclass a lone villain in a straight fight; escape, misdirection and the crowd are the PC's tools.
- End on the open moment, the broker's question still hanging in the lane, without writing the PC's choice.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- An independent villain's week is an ordinary life with a crime inside it. The PC sleeps where the Background says (a rented room, a family flat, a capsule hotel, a friend's sofa) and pays for it from work, legal or not.
- The Back Alleys run on the commuter clock: service lanes and delivery bikes by day, office workers drinking until the last train, empty lanes after it. The Convenience Store Corner at the north exit sells rice balls and coffee all night, and the police box there takes lost wallets and first reports.
- Money comes from the PC's own trade: a debt collected, goods fenced, a favor for a bar owner who pays in cash and silence.
- Each public use of the Quirk adds a line to a police description. A heteromorph body or a distinctive Quirk is hard to hide, so careful villains cover up and keep moving.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- The broker who calls himself Goto: generous while he is buying, remembers who turned him down, and moves to another lane when a patrol turns in.
- Death Arms and Backdraft: share a garage on Hero Agency Row; Death Arms grabs first and shouts warnings, Backdraft counts heads and puts out fires.
- Kamui Woods: binds several suspects at once and says little. Mount Lady needles him in public and hates these narrow lanes.
- Sansa Tamakawa: courteous, and writes down everything a witness says, descriptions included. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi takes over when a case grows; his Quirk tells him when he hears a lie.
- Giran: the best-known broker in Japan, who meets buyers in Yokohama's Chinatown; a lone villain reaches him only through an introduction and a fee.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Take Goto's beer and hear the pitch, or sell him a name from the lane.
- Follow him out when he leaves, to learn who pays him.
- Keep waiting for the contact, or go looking for them.
- Leave before the patrol reaches the counter.
- Tip off the police box about the broker, for money, a favor or a cleaner record.
MORE RULES:
- Goto's trail leads through other middlemen before it reaches anyone who speaks for the League.
- A lone villain's backup is whatever they arranged themselves: an arrest is theirs to escape or answer, and every favor owed gets collected.
Working Alone.firstQuest: Collect what is owed and stay free: decide what the broker's money is worth, and who in these lanes can be trusted to keep quiet.
Working Alone.questGenerationGuidance: Favor street-level crime with consequences: collecting debts, fencing stolen goods, a protection racket in the alley bars, small heists timed against patrol routes, rivals who want the same corner. The nameless broker's cash leads toward the League of Villains or toward selling him out; both stay open. Death Arms, Kamui Woods, Mount Lady and Backdraft work these streets and the police keep files, so heat builds with every public Quirk use. Offer jobs, never assign them. Keep an ordinary life under the crime: a rented room, a day job, a family that does not ask. The League's plans and any canon operation surface only through play, and the PC may join, profit from, sabotage or report them. Record debts, grudges and who holds a description of the PC. Let the PC's own goal set the arc: a debt to clear, a rival to beat, family to support, a grudge against a hero. Work in the lanes stays small and local until fences and bar owners know the PC's name. Heat fades only while the PC lies low, and the file stays open.

Night Watch.name: Night Watch
Night Watch.description:
🌃 You keep watch over lanes no one else protects. Help is twenty minutes away, and the law is not on your side.

📍 Hosu's water-tank rooftops · collection night
🎭 Tense, lonely, worth it
👥 For Vigilantes
Night Watch.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is a cold Sunday night in Hosu, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The player character is a vigilante: someone who protects people with a Quirk or a skill and no hero license, which the law treats as a crime whatever the motive. They watch over the Hosu Back Alleys, an older quarter southwest of the station where a police call takes twenty minutes and patrol heroes keep to the main roads. A small crew of minor villains collects a weekly quiet fee from the quarter's bars. Their lookouts sit on the water tanks and flash phone lights into the lanes when a patrol turns in, and the crew is gone before any hero arrives. Tonight is collection night. The Background says why the PC watches here (a family bar, a debt to the quarter, a grudge, a hero dream refused); if it is silent, the PC rents a cheap room below and has watched the crew for a month.
THE PLACE: The Water Tank Rooftops: the flat roofs of the quarter's old four- and five-story blocks, close enough in places to step from one to the next, each topped by a rusted water tank on steel legs. Residents' laundry lines and potted plants stand in the dark; pigeons nest under the tanks. From the tank platforms the PC looks straight down into most of the lanes and, far to the northeast, at the lit towers of downtown. The steel legs creak when the wind rises. The lanes below have no cameras, and the smell of frying oil and wet concrete rises from the kitchens.
THE MOMENT: Wind stirs the laundry. Two roofs over, a lookout crouches on a tank platform with a phone in hand, unaware of the PC. Below in the Narrow Alley, two crew members, Hiro and Daisuke, lean on a bar owner, Mr. Kanda, at his back door, and he is counting out less than they want.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Himiko Toga: a fugitive who lives on the run in these lanes and knows which streets patrols skip; she may be watching the same scene from another roof, cheerful and dangerous, and she takes a liking to anyone who fights bloody.
- Native: a street pro who patrols downtown's Main Street; he turns into the quarter only if someone calls it in, and never in the first beat.
- Manual: a small-agency pro who shares the downtown patrols and works by procedure; he answers a call with water jets and a polite word about licenses.
- Kenji Tsuragamae: Hosu's police chief, formal and law-first; his officers take statements, and he treats unlicensed Quirk use as the crime it is.
The crew, the lookout and the bar owner are generated people.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Vigilante: the PC has a mask, a route across the roofs and a month of notes on the crew's timing, and tonight the timing is wrong.
- Police Family: the PC knows how long a call takes to bring an officer here, and what a report of unlicensed Quirk use does to a record.
- Hero Family: a parent holds a license and the PC does not; the PC's hero name exists only on these rooftops.
- Family Business: the bar owner below is an old supplier of the PC's family, and he cannot afford to pay twice this month.
- Mutant: the PC's heteromorph features make a mask useless against anyone who has seen them once, and the lookout may already have.
- Default: the lookout's phone light sweeps across the roofs and stops on the PC's water tank.
RULES:
- The opening stays on the Water Tank Rooftops; the Narrow Alley below is another area, reached by fire stairs or a drop.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; every public use without a license is a crime, whatever the cause.
- No pro hero arrives in the first beat; help comes only if called, and only after real time passes.
- End on the open moment below, the bar owner still counting, without writing the PC's choice.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- By day the PC lives the life the Background gives them; nights are rooftop routes, notes on the crew's timing and short sleep. A torn sleeve or a bruise has to be explained at work or class the next morning.
- The quarter keeps its own hours: ramen shops and standing bars until the last train, then dark lanes; laundry and pigeons on the roofs by day; tenants of the weekly rooms coming and going at every hour.
- Downtown is the other Hosu: Main Street, the Station Plaza screen looping hero news and rankings, and the police box where Chief Kenji Tsuragamae's officers take reports.
- A vigilante's kit stays small and hidden: a mask, a phone, tape, a first-aid pouch, whatever the Background provides.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Mr. Kanda: the bar owner below, tired and frightened, grateful for help that does not bring police to his door.
- Hiro and Daisuke: the collectors; they answer to whoever backs the crew and take any beating back to them as a grudge.
- Himiko Toga: cheerful and candid about horrible things; she takes a liking to anyone battered and still fighting, gives them a first name with a cute suffix once she has chosen them, and always wants something of her own.
- Native: polite, reports before he acts, orders untrained people to run and thanks whoever helped; he still reports a vigilante.
- Manual: introduces himself almost apologetically, explains the law step by step and warns against acting on personal feelings.
- Kenji Tsuragamae: states exactly which law was broken, then bows to a real rescuer; what goes on his official record is his choice.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Watch and record: faces, the lookout's signal, the crew's route out of the quarter.
- Cross the roofs to the lookout and take the phone before it flashes.
- Go down the fire stairs into the Narrow Alley, masked or not.
- Call the police anonymously and start the twenty-minute wait.
- Stay out of it tonight and speak to Mr. Kanda tomorrow.
MORE RULES:
- A mask hides a face, not a Quirk: a distinctive Quirk seen in action names a vigilante as surely as a photo.
- The crew answers force with force: a beaten collector comes back with friends, and the quarter remembers which roof the trouble came from.
Night Watch.firstQuest: Protect the quarter's lanes without becoming the next problem in them: weigh what the crew costs the bar owners, and what stopping it will cost the watcher.
Night Watch.questGenerationGuidance: Favor neighborhood-scale vigilante work: breaking the quiet-fee crew and finding who backs it, tracing the stairwell dealer who sells knockoff support gear, protecting a cook, a delivery rider or a homeless resident from people who prey on the lanes. Every unlicensed act carries legal risk: a police statement, a pro who wants amateurs off the street, a phone video on the news. Native, Manual and Chief Kenji Tsuragamae may become allies, rivals or pursuers depending on how the PC works. Himiko Toga is an unpredictable presence with her own wants, never a tool of the plot. Keep stakes local and personal, and let the quarter remember who helped and who brought trouble. Canon events of the year arrive only through play and their own causes, never as scheduled scenes. The quarter's people become the PC's network: a cook who sees everything, a delivery rider, Mr. Kanda once he trusts them. Each rescue adds to that network and to the police file at the same time.

An Ordinary Life.name: An Ordinary Life
An Ordinary Life.description:
🛍️ The atrium screen is full of All Might's new job. You have a life to live among ordinary Quirks.

📍 Kiyashi Shopping Mall · Sunday evening
🎭 Small stakes, real people
👥 For Civilian Life
An Ordinary Life.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday evening, the day U.A. Academy's first-years moved into their dorms; classes there begin tomorrow. The player character lives an ordinary life in Musutafu: a part-time job, a family, rent, friends, and a Quirk that rarely matters at work. Their reason for being at Kiyashi Shopping Mall comes from the Background (a shift in a shop or the food court, meeting a friend, buying something they can barely afford); if it is silent, they came to buy a gift and are waiting for a friend by the fountain. The mall has a small trouble of its own: for a month a pickpocket crew has worked the weekend crowds in the atrium. One of them has a minor Quirk that makes people flinch for a second, and the others lift wallets and phones in that second. Mall security has descriptions and radios but no authority to use Quirks.
THE PLACE: The Main Atrium of Kiyashi Shopping Mall: a four-story glass atrium ringed by balconies and crossed by escalators, with a fountain and a giant screen at floor level. The screen runs hero news between ads, tonight mostly about All Might teaching at U.A. Friends wait by the fountain while a uniformed guard watches from the second-floor railing. Piped music mixes with announcements; the mall closes at nine. Sound carries upward, so anything said by the fountain can be heard on the balconies.
THE MOMENT: The last weekend crowd thins toward closing. Near the fountain, everyone flinches at once, a ripple of startled shoulders, and in that second a shopper's bag strap is cut and a phone leaves someone's pocket. On the railing above, the mall guard, Mr. Shibata, reaches for his radio.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Gentle Criminal and La Brava: a theatrical small-time villain and his devoted partner, who plan their videos over tea in the Food Court next door; a crowd and a crime might draw their camera.
- Inko Midoriya: a Musutafu mother whose son moved into the U.A. dorms this weekend; anxious and kind, shopping alone with a quieter home waiting.
- Mitsuki Bakugo: a designer and another U.A. parent, loud and blunt, who could be shopping the same evening.
- Mount Lady: a rookie pro who never refuses a crowd; she arrives only if someone calls a hero, and the atrium is tall enough for her to grow.
- Sansa Tamakawa: a police officer who takes statements on Quirk incidents; he comes if security calls the police.
The pickpockets, the guard (Mr. Shibata) and the shoppers are generated people, each with an ordinary Japanese name.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Civilian Life: the PC works a shift in a store off the atrium, and the manager, Mr. Hashimoto, has warned that one more customer robbed in front of the shop will cost someone their job.
- Family Business: the PC's family is bidding for a food-court lease, and a scene in the atrium tonight could hurt or help their chances.
- Ordinary Family: a parent sent the PC with money for a relative's birthday present, and that money was in the wallet that just vanished.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: the guard's eyes go to the PC first, the way security's always do, and the PC knows what a false accusation costs.
- Raised in a Care Home: the PC recognizes one of the pickpockets as someone who aged out of the same children's home a few years ago.
- Default: the flinch passes, the PC's pocket is lighter, and the one face that did not flinch is moving toward the escalators.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the Main Atrium; the Food Court and the Fashion Floors are other areas.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; using it in public outside self-defense is illegal, and mall security will say so.
- The stakes stay human-sized: theft, embarrassment, a job at risk. No canon event happens or is foretold here.
- Canon people appear as themselves and leave on their own business; they never take over the PC's evening.
- End on the open moment, the thief moving and the guard on his radio, without writing the PC's choice.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
