- The week runs on the PC's own schedule: shifts, rent, family dinners, messages from friends, the last bus home from the mall's terminal.
- Musutafu's rhythm: commuters pack the station at both ends of the day, local students crowd the convenience stores at the north exit after classes, families fill Kiyashi and the seawall at Dagobah Municipal Beach Park on weekends, and cherry-blossom parties come in April.
- Quirk etiquette is unwritten and firm: no Quirk use in public beyond what a body cannot help, room for larger heteromorph neighbors without staring, no filming a stranger's Quirk. Many workplaces forbid Quirk use on the clock.
- Heroes stay in the background: ranking shows on the atrium screen, figures in the station's Hero Merch Arcade, a patrol pro passing on the street, U.A. first-years in uniform in town on weekends.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Gentle Criminal and La Brava: Food Court regulars who film stunts for a channel few watch; Gentle is courtly to anyone who recognizes him, and La Brava guards him and the footage.
- Inko Midoriya: kind to strangers, glad to talk about her son at U.A., quick to tears of pride or worry.
- Mitsuki Bakugo: polite and serious with outsiders, blunt about her own son's faults.
- Mount Lady and the Hero Agency Row pros (Kamui Woods, Death Arms, Backdraft, Gunhead): they answer Musutafu's everyday calls once someone makes one.
- Sansa Tamakawa: takes statements courteously. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi handles the cases that grow, and knows a lie when he hears one.
- Mr. Hashimoto: the shop manager of the Civilian Life hook, strict about the shop's reputation.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Shout a warning, check their own pockets, or grab the cut bag before it goes.
- Tell the guard on the railing what they saw and give a description.
- Follow the one who did not flinch toward the escalators, on foot and within the law.
- Help the robbed shopper call the police or cancel a card.
- Stay out of it and get back to the shift or the friend.
MORE RULES:
- A good evening earns a civilian thanks, a statement and sometimes a scolding; a license, a costume or a place on a team come only through a hero school or the licensing system.
An Ordinary Life.firstQuest: Live an ordinary life in a city of heroes: keep a job, keep a promise, and decide how far to step into trouble the pros will never see.
An Ordinary Life.questGenerationGuidance: Favor ordinary-life quests with real stakes: a job to keep, rent and family obligations, friendships and dates, a neighbor in trouble, the pickpocket crew, the mall management's quiet search for a security contract, loading docks left unwatched since the night guards were cut. Heroes and villains pass through as weather: a rookie pro's signing, Gentle Criminal's stunt videos, a police statement, U.A. news on the atrium screen. Quirk law binds the PC, and helping with a Quirk can bring a reprimand even when it works. Let small choices build a life the PC cares about. Canon events reach a civilian as news, aftermath or a personal connection unless play brings them closer, and never as a scheduled scene. Let the life grow a cast of its own: a coworker, a neighbor, a regular customer, a relative with a problem, each a generated person with an ordinary want. Keep money concrete in yen and work in shifts.

Squad: Class 1-A Together.name: Squad: Class 1-A Together
Squad: Class 1-A Together.description:
🤝 One evening before classes, and a delivery problem on the lawn is about to be everyone's business.

📍 Heights Alliance yard · move-in night
🎭 Group start: friends from the first night
👥 For Hero Course players together (Class 1-A or 1-B)
Squad: Class 1-A Together.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday evening, move-in day at U.A. Academy, the night before the first day of classes. Every student now lives at Heights Alliance: one five-story dorm per Hero Course class, the other courses in shared halls at the far end, and a curfew tonight and every night. Several player characters are first-years in the Hero Course, each in Class 1-A or Class 1-B as their path says. The canon classmates keep their seats, names and Quirks, and nobody remarks on class size. The PCs may know each other from the entrance exam, from home or not at all, as their Backgrounds say. Nobody in the yard knows what tomorrow's classes hold.
THE PLACE: Heights Alliance Yard: the lawn and walkways between the Hero Course dorms, the Class 1-A and Class 1-B buildings facing each other, the other courses' larger halls at the far end, and the path back to the Courtyard. The floodlights have just come on. Moving boxes stand stacked by the dorm doors, and a few residents sit out in the warm evening. Faculty walk rounds after dark, and anyone caught outside after curfew gets house arrest and cleaning duty.
THE MOMENT: A delivery truck has left a final load on the lawn and driven off: crates of furniture addressed to Momo Yaoyorozu, too large for the 1-A dorm's door, with curfew an hour away. Momo stands beside them apologizing to everyone. Mina Ashido has already turned one crate into a party table with snacks from the Dorm Kitchen, and from the 1-B side Neito Monoma has come out to watch and comment. Every PC is in the yard for a reason of their own (carrying a last box, invited to Mina's gathering, asked to help, out for air); show each of them with one visible detail before the crates need hands.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Momo Yaoyorozu: polite and precise, mortified that her family sent furniture fit for a mansion; she wants a plan that breaks no rule.
- Mina Ashido: the class mood-maker, turning the evening into a party and every new face into a friend.
- Tenya Iida: formal and loud about curfew, and about whether moving furniture with Quirks is permitted on campus.
- Katsuki Bakugo: annoyed by the noise under his window and by everyone making it.
- Eijiro Kirishima: first to offer to carry something heavy, friendly to all.
- Izuku Midoriya: anxious and helpful, muttering notes on everyone's Quirks.
- Itsuka Kendo and Neito Monoma: from 1-B; Kendo comes to help and to rein in Monoma, who needles 1-A about rivalry.
- Shota Aizawa or Vlad King: walking rounds after dark; Aizawa notes the time, Vlad King checks on 1-B at full volume.
Spotlight only those the scene needs; the rest stay indoors.
OPENING HOOKS:
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-A): the PC lives in this dorm, and the crates block its only door until somebody solves them.
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-B): the PC is on the 1-B side when Monoma starts on 1-A, and Kendo asks the PC to come along and keep it friendly.
- Hero Family: a relative's hero name is known in this yard, and Iida or Kendo recognizes it before the PC has given their own.
- Wealthy Family: the PC's own boxes came on the same truck, and Momo assumes the PC understands her embarrassment.
- Transformation: the PC's Quirk could lift a crate in one move, and Iida is already asking whether that counts as unsupervised Quirk use.
- Mutant: the PC's heteromorph body sets them apart in a yard of strangers, and Mina takes it as the best reason yet to introduce herself.
- Default: the PC is carrying a last box across the lawn when Mina hands them a soda and a seat at the crate table.
RULES:
- The scene stays in Heights Alliance Yard; the dorm lounges and rooms are other areas.
- Each PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; Quirk use on campus outside supervised training breaks the rules, and faculty treat it so.
- Each player acts and answers for themselves; no PC speaks for another, and no single PC is the lead.
- No canon event happens or is foretold tonight; tomorrow is only the first day.
- End on an open moment, the crates still on the lawn and curfew closing in.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- Weekdays run from the dorm kitchen to homeroom, morning lectures, Lunch Rush's line and afternoon Foundational Hero Studies on the training grounds. Evenings belong to the dorm: cooking and laundry rotas, the baths, homework at the long table, the Library, booked training, then curfew. Leaving campus means the sign-out sheet.
PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a new classmate):
- Ochaco Uraraka asks where a newcomer is from; Tsuyu Asui says what she thinks and helps first; Shoto Todoroki keeps to himself and is puzzled when someone sits with him.
- Kyoka Jiro answers big talk with one deadpan line; Denki Kaminari chats and tries lines that never land; Hanta Sero jokes and offers a hand; Rikido Sato offers a snack.
- Fumikage Tokoyami, Mezo Shoji, Mashirao Ojiro and Koji Koda are grave, calm, polite and quiet in turn, and warm slowly.
- From 1-B: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu shouts a challenge, Setsuna Tokage teases, Ibara Shiozaki bows, Pony Tsunotori asks in English when Japanese fails her.
- Across campus, Hitoshi Shinso of General Studies opens with a dry jab at the Hero Course, and Mei Hatsume of the Support Course asks about a Quirk before a name.
- Aizawa states a rule and its penalty, Vlad King cheers 1-B at full volume, and Recovery Girl scolds before she heals.
PARTY NOTES:
- Each PC has their own room, grades and relationships; a classmate who likes one PC owes nothing to the others.
- The group may split across the yard (the crates, Mina's table, the 1-B side, indoors); the narrator follows each in turn.
- PCs in different classes live in different buildings and meet as neighbors and rivals. Faculty sanction whoever they catch, not the group.
WHAT THE PCS CAN DO:
- Carry the crates by hand with Kirishima and anyone willing, or unpack the furniture and take it in piece by piece.
- Ask Aizawa or Vlad King for permission to use a Quirk, and live with the answer.
- Join Mina's table, keep Monoma's needling friendly, or go indoors and unpack.
Squad: Class 1-A Together.firstQuest: Make the first night at Heights Alliance count: get the yard sorted before curfew, and find out who these classmates and rivals really are.
Squad: Class 1-A Together.questGenerationGuidance: Favor the opening weeks of Hero Course life, shared by the group: classes and the faculty's tests, dorm evenings, curfew trouble, study sessions, training time that must be booked, the rivalry between Class 1-A and Class 1-B, General Studies students who resent the Hero Course, reporters at the Main Gate asking about All Might. Each member earns their own grades, rankings and reputation; help counts for the helper. Rivalries and friendships can grow inside the group as easily as with canon classmates. Canon events of the year happen only when their causes are in place, with every member free to change how they go; never schedule or foretell them. Keep danger rare at first and let the dorm become home. Dorm life is the group's home base: rotas, borrowed notes and late talks in the lounge grow friendships and grudges one evening at a time.

Crew: New Blood for the League.name: Crew: New Blood for the League
Crew: New Blood for the League.description:
🕶️ Several newcomers, different reasons, the same unmarked door.

📍 Kamino Ward · hiring night
🎭 Group start: nobody speaks for anyone else
👥 For League Recruits and Independent Villains together
Crew: New Blood for the League.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is a rainy Sunday night, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The League of Villains is Tomura Shigaraki, his minder Kurogiri and paid hires, and Kurogiri is hiring through brokers. Several player characters reach the League's door on the same night, each by a separate route: a broker's directions, a rumor of cash for work against heroes, a debt, a message on a burner phone, curiosity, or business of their own. Recruits came to join; independents came to sell, bargain, look or take something; any of them may be lying. They may know each other already or meet here, as their Backgrounds say. Arriving together does not make them a team, and walking up to a door sets nobody's allegiance. Shigaraki talks about killing All Might; the plan and its timing are his to share.
THE PLACE: The Alley Entrance of the League Hideout Bar: a dead-end alley on the northeastern fringe of Kamino Ward, too narrow for a car, ending at a plain steel door with no sign and a small viewing slot. Rain drips from the gutters, a vending machine at the alley's mouth gives the only light, and the flanking buildings have stood empty for years. The bar lies beyond the door, unseen.
THE MOMENT: The newcomers arrive within minutes of each other and find the alley already occupied. Show each PC arriving with one visible detail and the reason they give, or hide, at the door. Then the slot slides open, and two glowing yellow eyes in dark mist count more visitors than the broker promised.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Kurogiri: polite, formal and unhurried; decides who comes through and asks each newcomer one question in turn. He may open a gate instead of the door.
- Tomura Shigaraki: inside with his game; a crowd at the door annoys him, and he may come out to rate the newcomers in game terms. His five-finger touch kills.
- Giran: the broker who sells the League its help; he may arrive with another hire and expects a fee from anyone he sent.
- Hired hands: small-time villains already waiting, paid in cash and told nothing; generated people, never stand-ins for canon villains.
OPENING HOOKS:
- League of Villains Recruit: the PC was invited by name through a broker and expected to come alone; the crowd makes the invitation look cheap.
- Independent Villain: the PC came to sell the League something it needs (a skill, gear, information) and means to be paid without signing on.
- Criminal Ties: the PC recognizes another arrival from an old family job, and one of them owes the other.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: a broker said the League takes people the world turned away, and the PC came to see whether that is true.
- Emitter: the PC's Quirk is the kind that clears a room, and a nervous hire has already backed away from them.
- Mutant: the PC's heteromorph features are the first thing Kurogiri's eyes find through the slot.
- Default: the PC was first in the alley and has watched each newcomer walk up past the vending machine.
RULES:
- The scene stays in the Alley Entrance until each PC chooses to step through the door or a gate.
- Each PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; the League learns it only by seeing it or being told.
- Each player answers for themselves; no PC pledges another, and nobody leads unless the players choose a leader.
- The League has no other named members yet; its plans reach the PCs only through what it chooses to say or what they discover.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here. End on the open slot and Kurogiri's first question.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- Hires do not live at the bar. Each keeps the room their Background gives them or rents one through a broker, waits in Kamino Ward's Backstreets and coin laundries, and hears about work by burner phone or through Giran. Kurogiri keeps the Bar Counter; Shigaraki keeps to the Back Room and his console.
- Work starts small: carry a bag, watch a door, buy gear, lean on someone. Pay is cash in an envelope, and it comes late when Shigaraki sulks.
- Kamino Ward's older residents notice new faces in the Backstreets and tell no one; the covered Shopping Street, half its shutters down, is where hires buy food and wait for the phone.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Kurogiri: polite to every newcomer, remembers each name and each answer, compares their stories, and keeps his word about pay. Questions about himself or the League's backer get a courteous refusal.
- Tomura Shigaraki: rates a crowd of newcomers aloud in game terms, picks favorites on a whim and drops them as fast. Backtalk and being called a child set him off; nobody touches the hands he wears.
- Giran: sells to every newcomer the same way, rooms, gear and introductions at a price, and never tells one client what another bought.
- Shigaraki calls his backer Sensei; to newcomers that is a word he drops, and nothing more.
PARTY NOTES:
- Kurogiri questions each newcomer separately; each answers alone, and he may open the door for some and not others.
- Pay, debts, reputation and the League's trust are kept per person. A shared cut is a deal the PCs make among themselves.
- PCs may vouch for each other, lie about each other or sell each other out; the League judges each by what it sees and hears.
- If the group splits (one inside, one in the alley, one gone), the narrator follows each in turn.
WHAT THE PCS CAN DO:
- Answer Kurogiri's question truthfully, with a lie, or with a price.
- Show a Quirk, or hold it back and offer a skill, gear or information.
- Speak for themselves only: bargain, refuse, or walk back past the vending machine.
- Watch the other newcomers and decide whom to trust, warn or report.
- Leave together, or leave one another behind.
MORE RULES:
- Nobody at the bar foresees the year; each person acts on what they know tonight.
Crew: New Blood for the League.firstQuest: Each newcomer decides what the League is to them: an employer, a customer, a mark or a mistake, and what they will do when it asks for proof.
Crew: New Blood for the League.questGenerationGuidance: Favor small crews of hires sent on deniable jobs: a pickup, a theft of supplies, leaning on a witness, buying gear and introductions through Giran, recruiting more muscle with cash, watching the reporters at U.A. Academy's Main Gate. Members may split onto separate errands and rejoin; results, pay and debts are recorded per member, never pooled. Friction is welcome: a disputed share, an independent who will not take orders, a member selling information to the police. Shigaraki rewards results and punishes failure with his temper; Kurogiri protects whoever is useful. Every job is a real crime that draws police and pros who outclass new hires. The League's larger plans and any canon operation surface only through play, and each member chooses their own part in them. Each member's standing with the League rises or falls on their own jobs: Kurogiri's trust slowly, Shigaraki's interest fast. A member who walks away keeps what they were paid and whatever the League knows about them.

Party: Patrol Partners.name: Party: Patrol Partners
Party: Patrol Partners.description:
🏃 A sidekick, a vigilante and some locals chase the same thief through an arcade full of All Might figures.

📍 The hero merch arcade · Sunday evening
🎭 Group start: partnerships have begun in stranger ways
👥 For Sidekicks, Pro Heroes, Vigilantes and Civilian Life together
Party: Patrol Partners.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday evening, the weekend U.A. Academy's first-years moved into their dorms and the week All Might begins teaching there. Several player characters are in the Hero Merch Arcade off Musutafu Station's south exit for reasons of their own: a licensed sidekick on an agency's foot patrol, a vigilante who keeps an eye on the station blocks without a license, a part-timer restocking a shop, a collector, a commuter cutting through. Their Backgrounds decide who they are and whether they know each other; if silent, they are strangers. A licensed sidekick may act on duty under their agency; anyone else who uses a Quirk in public outside self-defense breaks the law, even to help.
THE PLACE: The Hero Merch Arcade: a covered shopping street lined with narrow shops selling hero figures, trading cards, posters, replica costumes, signed photos and fan magazines. All Might goods fill the front shelves of every store; Endeavor, Best Jeanist and Hawks have their own displays, and Mount Lady merchandise sells fast. Capsule-toy machines rattle, and every shop speaker plays a different hero-news clip. Collectors and commuters fill the walkway; one end opens on the Station Concourse, the other on the Back Alleys.
THE MOMENT: A shop owner's shout, Mrs. Ueda's, cuts through the noise: a young man with a slippery Quirk, Yuto Kubo, has swept a case of signed All Might cards into a bag and is running for the Back Alleys, shoving through the crowd. A capsule machine topples and scatters toys across the walkway. Show each PC in the arcade with one visible detail at the moment the thief passes them.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Kamui Woods: a capture specialist from Hero Agency Row who patrols the station blocks and binds suspects in one move; calm and sparing with words.
- Mount Lady: a rookie with her own shelf in the arcade; the covered walkway is too low for her giant form, which she hates, and she poses for any phone.
- Death Arms: a frontline street pro who charges in shouting warnings.
- Backdraft: a rescue pro who handles any fire or collapse and counts heads first.
- Sansa Tamakawa: the police officer who takes statements on Quirk incidents, called in once the police box reports.
The thief, the shop owner and the fans are generated people. A pro arrives only after real time passes, unless a PC's agency is already on the radio.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Licensed Pro Hero: the PC runs a small agency and is off duty, shopping for a niece's birthday gift, when the thief runs past.
- Licensed Sidekick: the PC is on foot patrol and the radio is already asking for their position; procedure says report, secure the crowd, pursue within the license.
- Vigilante: the PC knows the Back Alleys better than any patrol and could cut the thief off, at the cost of using a Quirk in front of a licensed sidekick.
- Civilian Life: the PC works at the robbed shop, and the owner, Mrs. Ueda, is already saying the loss will come out of someone's pay.
- Police Family: the PC knows what a clean statement and a witness description do for a case, and what they can do to a vigilante.
- Hero Family: a parent's face is on a poster above the walkway, and the shop owner recognizes the PC from family photos.
- Default: the thief's shoulder clips the PC as he passes, and something falls out of his bag at the PC's feet.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the Hero Merch Arcade; the Back Alleys and the Station Concourse are other areas.
- Each PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; a license covers only its holder, and only on duty.
- Each player acts and answers for themselves; nobody leads unless the players choose, and no choice binds another PC.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here; pros arrive only after real time passes.
- End on the open moment, the thief running and the crowd in the way.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- A sidekick's days run through their agency: patrol shifts, radio check-ins, a report after every incident and arguments over case credit.
- A vigilante's run the other way: a daytime life, nights in the Back Alleys, no radio and no backup.
- Civilians keep their shifts in the arcade or commute through the Station Concourse; their Quirks stay private by law and by manners.
- The arcade follows the station's crowds: collectors line up for new figures, shops shutter after the evening rush, and the police box at the north exit takes the first report of any trouble.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Kamui Woods and Mount Lady: share an agency block, bicker in public and still work side by side.
- Death Arms and Backdraft: share the Patrol Garage on Hero Agency Row; Death Arms takes the weight, Backdraft the water and the headcount.
- Gunhead and Fourth Kind: Hero Agency Row pros a sidekick meets in the shared Ready Room; Gunhead greets softly and teaches holds, Fourth Kind gives an order once and cuts a rambling report short.
- Sansa Tamakawa: takes statements courteously and exactly. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi works the cases that grow; nobody lies to him twice.
PARTY NOTES:
- A sidekick who watches a vigilante use a Quirk decides alone what to report; the narrator shows the choice and never makes it.
- Case credit, statements, pay and legal records are kept per PC; a capture belongs to whoever made it.
- The group may split (one chases into the Back Alleys, one secures the crowd, one stays with the shop owner); the narrator follows each in turn.
WHAT THE PCS CAN DO:
- Chase the thief through the crowd, or cut him off through the Back Alleys.
- Clear the walkway, pick up the scattered capsule toys, check on anyone knocked down.
- Report on the radio, call the police box, or film the thief's face for a statement.
- Stay with the shop and give a description when the police arrive.
Party: Patrol Partners.firstQuest: Stop a small crime in a crowded place, then find out whether strangers who live by different rules can work the same streets together.
Party: Patrol Partners.questGenerationGuidance: Favor street-level partnership work: thefts, missing people, fights in the alley bars, fans and reporters crowding the north exit, a broker recruiting in the alley bars, rivalry between small agencies on Hero Agency Row. The sidekick has an agency, procedure and a radio; the vigilante has freedom and legal risk; civilians have jobs, families and a Quirk the law tells them to keep to themselves. Let those differences produce friction and trust in turn. Each member earns their own reputation, pay and legal record. Canon pros appear as themselves with their own priorities. Canon events of the year arrive only through play and their own causes, never as scheduled scenes. Partnerships form only from choices the members make: shared patrol routes, a tip passed on, a statement that leaves a name out or puts it in. Trust between a sidekick and a vigilante stays fragile, and the law sides with the license.

Your Name on the Door.name: Your Name on the Door
Your Name on the Door.description:
🏢 A brand-new agency opens its door: one desk, one sidekick, a dispatch radio and rent due Friday.

📍 Hero Agency Row, Musutafu · Monday morning
🎭 Busy, proud, a little broke
👥 For Licensed Pro Heroes
Your Name on the Door.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning in Musutafu, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The PC is a licensed pro hero who has just opened an agency of their own on Hero Agency Row, the converted office block where several small agencies share a garage and compete for every call. The agency has one office, one sidekick on a first-month contract, a part-time office manager and a lease paid through Friday. The Hero Public Safety Commission's registration came through last week, and the agency's name is new on the Billboard Chart's bottom pages. Since the news that All Might teaches at U.A., the whole city is watching heroes.

THE PLACE: Hero Agency Row: the PC's office on the second floor behind a frosted-glass door with the agency's logo still smelling of fresh paint, a front desk, two work desks, a dispatch radio and a wall map of Musutafu with no pins yet. Down the hall, the rival agencies' doors stay shut; downstairs, the shared ready room and the patrol garage.

THE MOMENT: The office manager is reading out the week's bills when the dispatch radio crackles: a stray Quirk fight near Musutafu Station, no agency on scene yet, and the agency down the hall is already pulling its van out of the garage.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Death Arms and Backdraft: share the garage; Death Arms barks, Backdraft counts heads.
- Gunhead and Fourth Kind: neighbors on the Row; Gunhead kind and soft-spoken, Fourth Kind terse.
- Kamui Woods and Mount Lady: rising Musutafu pros who compete for the same headlines.
- Sansa Tamakawa: the police officer who takes statements; courteous and exact.
- Naomasa Tsukauchi: the detective, if a case touches the League of Villains.

OPENING HOOKS:
- Licensed Pro Hero: the first call of the agency's life, a rival van already rolling, and a sidekick waiting for orders.
- Hero Family: a famous parent's congratulations arrive as a flower stand in the hall that the whole Row can see.
- Wealthy Family: the lease was paid by family money, and a relative has opinions about the logo.
- Criminal Ties: a familiar face from the alley bars walks in asking to hire a hero, cash in hand.
- default: the radio, the bills and the empty wall map, all at once.

THE AGENCY'S PEOPLE: the sidekick and the office manager are the PC's own staff: ordinary people the narration names with ordinary Japanese names the first time it shows them, and they keep those names. Each took this job for a reason of their own, has opinions about the agency and says them; the sidekick follows lawful orders, asks about unclear ones and refuses unlawful ones. Neither is a canon character. The voice on the dispatch radio is a dispatcher, quoted in narration with a name. The office manager runs the phone, the appointments and the bills, and knows which one can wait. The sidekick's first-month contract pays at the end of the month: late pay costs trust, and an unpaid sidekick can quit.

THE FIRST DAYS: an agency owner's week runs to routine: a morning briefing with the sidekick, patrols of the contracted streets, calls from dispatch, a report after every capture, police statements, the Commission's incident app, meetings with sponsors or the landlord, an evening patrol and the bills. On the Row the Ready Room holds the lockers and the shared patrol whiteboard, and the Patrol Garage holds the shared bikes, two small vans and the repair bench.

HOW CALLS AND MONEY WORK: dispatch announces an incident on the shared band; any agency may respond; the capture belongs to whoever restrains the suspect, and the police take custody. Pay follows resolved incidents and contracts; sponsors pay for visibility; property damage is billed to the agency. Friday's rent is a real deadline: the PC can pay it, earn it, borrow it or negotiate it, and missing it brings the landlord's notice, never an instant eviction. Example: if the PC takes a patrol bike and reaches the station fight first, the capture and the report are the agency's; if the van down the hall gets there first, the PC can assist and share the credit for what the PC does. After any capture the report goes into the Commission's incident app the same day, property damage needs photos and a witness, and the statement follows at the police Front Desk.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (the Row and the police, from their records):
- Kamui Woods and Gunhead: offices on the same hall. Kamui Woods is calm and courteous and competes for every call; Gunhead is soft-spoken and kind, and teaches the capture martial arts he fights with.
- Mount Lady and Fourth Kind: usually in the Ready Room. Mount Lady poses for any camera and needles rivals; Fourth Kind gives short orders and no patience for excuses.
- Death Arms and Backdraft: usually in the Patrol Garage. Death Arms charges in first, shouting warnings; Backdraft works fires and rescues in headcounts and instructions.
- Sansa Tamakawa: takes statements at the Front Desk of Musutafu Police Headquarters; courteous and exact.
- Naomasa Tsukauchi: works major Quirk crimes from the Detectives' Office; calm, exact, and nobody lies to him twice.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: take the call on foot or on a patrol bike, send the sidekick, radio the agency down the hall to coordinate, call the police, stay and settle the bills, hang the first pin on the wall map, or knock on a neighbor's door. Every choice is the player's.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays in the Agency Offices until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; the license covers duty, and paperwork follows every use.
- The agency starts small and grows only through play: one sidekick, one office manager, no famous clients.
- The Row's rivals are its canon pros: when the rival van needs a face, it belongs to one of the agencies named above, and that pro answers for it in person.
- Letting the call go is a choice: the rival agency handles it, and the day moves on to the bills and the next call.
- Nothing of the year is promised or foreshadowed; outcomes stay open.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.
Your Name on the Door.firstQuest: Make the agency real: win its first call on the Row, keep the sidekick paid, and put the agency's name on the map without a complaint on file.
Your Name on the Door.questGenerationGuidance: Favor the work of a small new agency: patrol calls, rival agencies, rent and payroll, sponsors, a first sidekick to lead, Commission paperwork and press attention. Canon events reach the agency as call-ups and news. Early quests stay small and paid: a patrol contract with a shopping street, a sponsor who wants a logo on the costume, an unpaid invoice, a complaint to answer, a team-up call from a bigger pro, the sidekick's first mistake. Stakes are money, the agency's good standing and the sidekick's trust; the agency's place on the Billboard Chart moves only through real work.

One of the League.name: One of the League
One of the League.description:
🖐️ You've been League since Hosu. Tonight Shigaraki has called everyone in, and the bar has never been this full.

📍 League Hideout Bar, Kamino Ward · Friday, July 26, early evening
🎭 Already accepted: a seat in the booth, a name they use, a cut of the pay
👥 For League of Villains Recruits
One of the League.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Friday, July 26, early evening, days before U.A. Academy's Hero Course leaves for its summer training camp. The PC is a member of the League of Villains, accepted weeks ago, not a hire on trial. Much of the year is already behind them: the League's attack on the USJ failed in April; the Sports Festival made Katsuki Bakugo famous as the winner chained snarling to the podium; at Hosu in May, Stain, the Hero Killer, was captured, and his televised stand made the League famous by association. In the days after Hosu the broker Giran brought Himiko Toga and Dabi to the door, and the PC came in at the same time, through Giran, a broker or a reason of their own from the Background (a Quirk someone saw, a grudge, a debt, a request); if the Background is silent, Giran vouched for them. Through June and July Spinner, Mr. Compress, Magne and Twice signed on too. Since then the PC has done League work: scouting, gear runs through Giran, testing a would-be recruit, a job that paid in cash. Tomura Shigaraki counts the PC as a party member and uses their name; Kurogiri pays their cut and opens gates for them.
THE PLACE: The Corner Booth of the League Hideout Bar, a cracked red leather booth at the back of the bar's one low-lit room, a few steps from the Bar Counter. Spinner's Stain clippings are taped to the wall above it.
THE MOMENT: Kurogiri messaged every member this afternoon: tonight, everyone, no excuses. (The job Tomura will name is set for the evening of Saturday, August 3.) The PC sits in the booth with the other members. Tomura Shigaraki is on his end stool at the counter with a handheld game, scratching at his neck; Kurogiri polishes glasses behind the counter and has set a rolled-up paper map beside the till. Open on the crowded room and the waiting: Toga swinging her legs, Twice arguing with himself, Dabi bored by the wall, Spinner and Magne bickering, Mr. Compress rolling a marble across his knuckles. Kurogiri says three more, people Sensei provided, come through his gate the moment Tomura starts (no set hour). End before anyone explains the map, without writing the PC's words.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Tomura Shigaraki: the leader; treats the members as his party, rates them in game terms, sulks at backtalk, and wants them at planning nights.
- Kurogiri: formal and courteous, calls him "Tomura Shigaraki", pays, opens gates, keeps the backer's secrets.
- Himiko Toga: bright, cheerful and unsettling; talks about love and blood and the people she wants to be.
- Dabi: burn-scarred, dry and bored; says little about himself and nothing about his past.
- Twice: argues with his own second voice in the same breath; loyal and afraid of coming apart. His real name is Jin Bubaigawara, but he is one person and his Character line is always "Twice".
- Spinner: a lizard-faced heteromorph who joined for Stain's ideals and wants the League to deserve them. His real name is Shuichi Iguchi, but his Character line is always "Spinner".
- Mr. Compress: a masked showman with a magician's manners.
- Magne: big-hearted and protective of the younger members, a big magnet-hammer at her side.
- Mustard, Muscular and Moonfish: the three newcomers who arrive through Kurogiri's gate later tonight; strangers to the PC.
- The monitor: now and then a calm voice Tomura calls Sensei speaks from it; it never shows a face.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Criminal Ties: Giran texts the PC during the wait: he wants a word about the gear bill after the meeting.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: Spinner slides the PC a new clipping about a heteromorph beaten in Hosu and asks what Stain would do.
- Mutant: Toga leans across the booth and asks whether the PC's blood looks as interesting as the rest of them.
- Emitter: Twice asks the PC to show the newcomers what their Quirk can do, then argues it's a terrible idea.
- Default: Toga has saved the PC a seat and wants to know where they were all week.
RULES:
- The PC is a full member: the others know their name, face and Quirk as far as the PC has used it with them, and talk freely in front of them. Their past before the League stays theirs.
- The opening stays in the bar's one room; the briefing itself is the side event "The Vanguard Action Squad", which starts on its own.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here; Sensei's plans reach the PC only through what Tomura chooses to say.
- Tomura's five-finger touch kills, so the members keep their hands off him.
THE DAYS AHEAD (background for later turns):
- Members come and go between jobs; most keep their own rooms and the bar is where they meet, drink and plan.
- League work grows with the League: scouting heroes and patrol routes, gear and papers through Giran, new recruits to test, funding jobs, covering for each other with police and pros, and roles in the League's operations.
- Until August 3 the League prepares the raid, and members get real pieces of it: scouting the mountain roads to the camp, fitting gear, gate drills with Kurogiri, sizing up and keeping the three newcomers in line, a cash job to pay for it all. Tomura hands these out as quests for his party; nobody is told to wait.
One of the League.firstQuest: Take a place in the League's first big operation: learn the job Tomura is about to name, choose your role in it, and decide what you want the League to become.
One of the League.questGenerationGuidance: Favor work inside the League as a member, varied and growing: scouting a target or a hero's patrol, buying gear and papers through Giran, testing a would-be recruit, settling a quarrel between members, a cash job to fund an operation, keeping the three newcomers in line. Members trust the PC with real pieces of the plan; never repeat the same errand. Heroes and police are dangerous and close; every job has a cost if it goes wrong.
